findings.evidence: The text states 'Par défaut, vous ne pourrez pas accéder au site' (By default, you will not be able to access the site) if you don't accept cookies, and the only way to refuse cookies is through the 'S'abonner et refuser les cookies' link which requires subscription.
findings.explanation: The user cannot access the site without either accepting cookies or subscribing, which is an action they did not ask for. This forces the user to either accept cookies or take an additional unwanted action (subscription) to refuse them.

findings.evidence: The 'Accepter' button is a large, prominent blue button, while the option to refuse cookies is a small text link 'S'abonner et refuser les cookies' at the top right of the modal.
findings.explanation: The primary action the business wants (accepting cookies) is visually dominant, while the user's desired action (refusing cookies) is presented as a less prominent text link, making it harder to find and use.

findings.evidence: The 'Reject' option is not visible as a button in the cookie banner; the text states 'You can select 'Accept' to consent to these uses, 'Reject' to decline these uses or click on 'More options' to review your options,' but the 'Reject' button is not displayed in the visible portion of the banner, making it less accessible than the 'Accept' option.
findings.explanation: The 'Reject' option is not presented as a visible button in the cookie banner, forcing users to look for it or potentially miss it, which hinders the goal of refusing non-essential cookies.

findings.evidence: The 'S'abonner et refuser les cookies' link requires the user to subscribe to refuse cookies, which is an extra step not related to the cookie consent decision.
findings.explanation: The design adds an unnecessary step (subscription) to the process of refusing cookies, which does not serve the user's goal of simply managing cookie preferences.

legal.title: Consent required for non-essential cookies
legal.summary: Directive 2002/58/EC requires prior consent before storing or reading non-essential trackers on a user's device (transposed in France by Art. 82 of the Loi Informatique et Libertés).

legal.title: Refusing cookies must be as easy as accepting them
legal.summary: The CNIL guidelines and recommendation on cookies require that refusing be as simple as accepting. In January 2022 the CNIL fined Google €150M and Facebook €60M because refusing took more clicks than accepting.

legal.title: Withdrawing consent must be as easy as giving it
legal.summary: Regulation (EU) 2016/679 requires that it be as easy to withdraw consent as to give it.

legal.title: Unfair Commercial Practices Directive
legal.summary: Prohibits misleading and aggressive commercial practices, including non-contractual barriers to terminating a contract.

legal.title: Ban on deceptive interface design by online platforms
legal.summary: Regulation (EU) 2022/2065 forbids online platforms from designing interfaces that deceive or manipulate users, including giving more prominence to certain choices, repeatedly requesting a choice already made, and making termination harder than subscribing.
